name: MathlibAnnex.PluckerRecovery.nonempty_limitCertificate_of_pluckerBodies_eq
title: A volume-normalized linear contraction obtained by a limit

content.display_title: A volume-normalized linear contraction obtained by a limit
content.one_sentence_role: Takes a compact operator limit preserving the exact volume equation.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$ and $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the reference sup norm and standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. The continuous norms $p,q$ have fixed positive comparison constants
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty,\qquad
a_q\|x\|_\infty\le q(x)\le b_q\|x\|_\infty.$$
Set $K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\}$, $K_q=\{x:q(x)\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)$, $v_q=\lambda(K_q)$, as positive finite real numbers. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$, let $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$ be its matrix in the standard bases. The minor-coordinate space has one coordinate for each increasing $n$-tuple $I$ of distinct rows from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and
$$\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*}).$$
Define the signed generator set and its real convex hull by
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal G_p^N
 &=\left\{\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A):\begin{array}{l}
       A:V\to\mathbb R^N\text{ is real linear},\ \sigma\in\{1,-1\},\\
       \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V)
       \end{array}\right\},\\
\mathcal P_p^N&=\operatorname{conv}_{\mathbb R}\mathcal G_p^N.
\end{aligned}$$
Define $\mathcal G_q^N,\mathcal P_q^N$ in the same way using $q,v_q$. The generators are vectors of minors, not linear maps. Assume $\mathcal P_p^N=\mathcal P_q^N$ for every $N$. There is one real linear $L:V\to V$ with
$$\forall x,\ q(Lx)\le p(x),\qquad L(K_p)\subseteq K_q,\qquad
v_p|\det L|=v_q,$$
$$\det L\ne0,\qquad L\text{ injective and surjective}.$$
content.assumptions: The positive-dimensional coordinates, norm models and equality of every finite body are the inputs. No distortion parameter is supplied.
content.conclusion: The same real linear bijection $L$ is contractive from the norm $p$ to the norm $q$ and has the exact determinant-volume normalization. Only ball inclusion is asserted here; equality of the two ball images is proved separately.
content.proof_summary: Choose vanishing distortions, bound the maps in one compact operator ball, and pass the estimate and determinant equation to the same subsequence limit.

proof_steps.text:
**Choose and bound the sequence.** Set $\varepsilon_k=1/(k+2)$. For each $k$, [linear recovery](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L989-L995) at the positive parameter $\varepsilon_k$ gives
$$(1-\varepsilon_k)q(L_kx)\le p(x),\qquad v_p|\det L_k|=v_q.$$
Because $0<\varepsilon_k\le1/2$ and $q\ge0$,
$$\frac12q(L_kx)\le(1-\varepsilon_k)q(L_kx)\le p(x),$$
$$a_q\|L_kx\|_\infty\le q(L_kx)\le2p(x)\le2b_p\|x\|_\infty.$$
Consequently $\|L_kx\|_\infty\le(2b_p/a_q)\|x\|_\infty$. These are [the half-distortion estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L1003-L1011) and [the reference-norm estimate](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/RecoveryCertificate.lean#L1013-L1023), applied to the selected certificates.

**Apply compactness in the operator space.** For real linear maps $T:V\to V$, use the reference operator norm $\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|x\|_\infty\le1}\|Tx\|_\infty$. All maps belong to the same closed operator ball $\{T:\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2b_p/a_q\}$. The real space of linear maps $V\to V$ is finite-dimensional, so this ball is compact. The [compact subsequence construction](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L148-L162) returns strictly increasing $k_j$ and one $L$ with $L_{k_j}\to L$ in operator norm. For each fixed $x$,
$$\|L_{k_j}x-Lx\|_\infty
\le\|L_{k_j}-L\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|x\|_\infty\longrightarrow0.$$
Strict increase gives $k_j\to\infty$ and hence $\varepsilon_{k_j}\to0$. In [compact subsequence selection](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Topology/Sequences.lean#L298-L300), the input sequence lies in one compact set in a first-countable space; the output is a limit in that set and a strictly increasing subsequence. The [continuous evaluation map and its RHS](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/360da6fa66c1273b76b6b2d8c5666fd5ac2e3b56/Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Bilinear.lean#L245-L256) is $\mathrm{ev}_x(T)=Tx$, giving the same pointwise limit.

**Pass the norm estimate to that limit.** Continuity of $q$ gives $q(L_{k_j}x)\to q(Lx)$. Therefore
$$(1-\varepsilon_{k_j})q(L_{k_j}x)\longrightarrow q(Lx).$$
Every term is at most $p(x)$, so $q(Lx)\le p(x)$. If $x\in K_p$, then $q(Lx)\le1$, giving $L(K_p)\subseteq K_q$. These are [the limit contraction](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L191-L211) and [its ball inclusion](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L214-L219).

**Pass the volume identity to the same map.** The determinant is continuous in the entries, so $\det L_{k_j}\to\det L$. Thus
$$v_p|\det L|
=\lim_{j\to\infty}v_p|\det L_{k_j}|=v_q.$$
This is [the limit determinant-volume equation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Plucker/LimitRecovery.lean#L237-L266). Since $v_q>0$, the determinant cannot vanish. It makes $L$ injective, and an injection from finite-dimensional $V$ to itself is surjective. Store this same $L$ in every field.

content.lean_realization_notes: The subsequence and its convergence are construction evidence, not extra public fields. Operator compactness uses the reference sup norm; contraction compares the stored norms $p,q$.
